name: MERIDIAN EMERGENCY BROADCAST AUTHORITY
creator: Meridian Municipal Governance Compact / HelixCorp Infrastructure Division (joint)
description: The official emergency broadcast system for GLMZ, MEBA transmits across all licensed neural feed channels, legacy video, audio, and public holographic displays during declared emergencies — chemical events, Behemoth incursion alerts from the Iowa border, major infrastructure failures, and corponation security lockdowns. Its broadcasts are characterized by a distinctive three-tone chime, a flat synthetic voice designated 'Caretaker,' and instruction sets that critics note are systematically more detailed for Tier 3-5 districts than for the Shelf. MEBA can override all licensed broadcast channels simultaneously.
medium: neural feed override, legacy audio/video, public holographic display, physical siren network
cultural_impact: MEBA is the only broadcast system legally authorized to reach every citizen regardless of subscription tier, making it the closest thing Meridian has to a shared civic voice — a fact that makes its differential coverage of Shelf emergencies all the more politically charged.
controversy: During the 2216 District 4 chemical fire, MEBA issued evacuation instructions that covered Tier 2-3 blocks but omitted the adjacent Shelf corridor for eleven minutes — a delay later attributed to 'mapping data latency.' Shelf Frequency filled the gap. The incident became a landmark case in ongoing litigation over MEBA's equal-access obligations.
story_hooks: MEBA issues an emergency alert for a threat that no one — not corporate security, not Shelf scouts, not independent monitors — can verify; either the system has been spoofed or something is happening that the corponations don't want publicly explained.
Someone has obtained the override credentials for MEBA's Caretaker voice synthesis and is planning to use them — the question is whether their message is a warning or a weapon.
An archival researcher discovers that MEBA's response logs from a 2201 Shelf disaster were retroactively altered; the original logs suggest a warning was issued, suppressed, and then erased.
